transcript:
User: Yeah, I got a voicemail from you people. This better be quick, I've got three jobs waiting.
Agent: Got it, I’ll keep this super quick.  

Was it the part about “not losing money from missed calls” that caught your ear, or something else in the voicemail?
User: I don't remember, my wife made me call. Is this some kind of scam?
Agent: Totally fair question — no, this isn’t a scam. We work with contractors so they don’t lose jobs when calls go to voicemail or get missed.  

Since your wife had you call, I’m guessing she’s seeing calls slip through — when you’re out on those three jobs, who usually answers your phone?
User: No one answers, and that's none of your business. Why do you even need to know that?
Agent: Mhm, I hear you — you’re busy and don’t want someone poking around in your business.  

Let me keep it simple: we set things up so when you can’t grab the phone, you still get the job and a booked appointment instead of a missed call — is that something you’d even want help with, or should I let you get back to your day?
User: Everyone claims they're the solution. How do I know this isn't just a waste of my time?
Agent: Yeah, I get that — everyone’s “the answer” until they waste your time.  

So… when a customer calls you now and no one picks up, do they usually leave a voicemail, or do they just hang up and disappear?
User: Most just hang up, and I've got jobs to get to. I don't have time for this.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — you’re slammed and most callers just bail.  

So when they hang up instead of leaving a message, do you think they usually call you back later, or do they just ring the next contractor on Google?
User: They probably just call the next guy. Everyone's got plumbing problems, why wait around?
Agent: Right, exactly — they’re not waiting, they’re just giving that money to the next guy.  

Rough guess: in a busy week, how many of those calls do you think hit voicemail or go unanswered — a couple a day, more, less?
User: I told you, I don't keep track of that. Why the insistence on numbers?
Agent: Gotcha, fair pushback — if you’re not counting, that’s your answer right there.  

So instead of numbers, let me ask it this way: if we could make sure those people who “just hang up” still turned into booked plumbing jobs without you touching the phone, is that actually worth fixing for you or not really?
User: Everyone promises that. I don't see how you can change human nature. I've heard it all before.
Agent: Totally get that — you’ve been pitched a lot, and people don’t suddenly become more patient just because some company calls you.  

So let me ask you this: if instead of hoping humans would wait, every time they called and you couldn’t answer, something automatically picked up, grabbed their info, and booked the job on your calendar… would that actually move the needle for you, or are you pretty much fine with how it is now?
User: Sounds too good to be true. And what's the catch? I don't buy quick fixes.
Agent: Yeah, makes sense — if it sounds like magic, it usually is.  

No fluff: would you be open to a quick look at how many jobs you’re likely losing off those hang-ups using *your* kind of numbers, or do you want to pass and keep it as-is?
User: I've heard enough. I don't have time for this. Bye.
Agent: Got it, I hear you. I’ll let you get back to your jobs — if you ever decide you’re tired of those hang-up calls turning into work for the next plumber, you can always give us another call. Have a good one.
